page: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v6 is an Edsv6-family memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 48 vCPUs and 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor with 24 physical cores and a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, this server features a 260 MB L3 cache. It includes 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The CPU architecture supports advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for accelerated tile and integer operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the E48ds_v6 demonstrates strong performance across multiple domains. It achieves top-tier results in Geekbench image processing and strong ratings in Geekbench multi-core, ray tracing, and software compilation tests. Memory performance is characterized by high read-only bandwidth for small cached blocks, though Passmark memory scores and large-block uncached read/write bandwidth remain in the average to weak ranges. The system also shows strong throughput in Redis SET operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and local storage-heavy tasks. The inclusion of Intel AMX instructions enables efficient CPU-based LLM inference, as evidenced by strong token generation speeds on small and medium models. However, the lack of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training. The server represents a resource-dense option for enterprise databases, caching layers, and software development pipelines that require a balance of high memory capacity and fast local NVMe storage.
